text:
maya: Hey team — noticed during the last onboard spike that ephemeral peering backoff was preempting tenant connections with lower priority. Customers on Dedicated saw their control-plane handshakes time out and got routed to the shared relay.

liam: I saw this too. Root cause appears to be the peering allocator doing aggressive backoff when the regional pool hits ephemeral IP exhaustion, and we treat all tenants equally in the allocator queue.

sasha: Can you paste the allocator logs?

maya: snippet from connector logs: `PeeringAllocator: pool=regional-a free=2 pending=18 backoff=exp(2) jitter=0.2 tenant=customer-42` — you'll see the backoff ramp.

liam: Right — two problems: 1) we don't encode tenant priority (enterprise vs self-serve) into the scoring function, and 2) backoff is global for all requests so it ends up preempting pinned sessions.

alex: Quick brainstorm: add a per-tenant priority score and a soft-affinity bucket. When pool low, prefer draining lower-priority and keep pinned sessions open for high-priority tenants.

sasha: I like priority + soft-affinity. Tradeoffs: more state in allocator, potential route thrash if priorities change, and slightly higher complexity in reconnect logic. Also need to ensure we don't starve small tenants entirely.

maya: Agreed. Proposal sketch: score = base_priority * (1 + pinned_bonus) - recent_failures_penalty. When allocating ephemeral peer, sort by score desc. Add a small token for pinned sessions (pinned_bonus = 0.5).

liam: Implementation notes: connector exposes headers and labels for priority. Example: `X-Redwood-Priority: tier=enterprise; pinned=true` and the allocator will read the labels from the onboarding request.

alex: Will need to update operator to persist pinned flags and to hold ephemeral lease extensions for pinned sessions. Otherwise allocator will still evict them on next sweep.

ops-runner: deploy-bot: rolling cut planned?

deploy-bot: @ops-runner started canary rollout: connectors-v2 -> staging (5%) at 2025-12-01T18:02:00Z.

liam: Also need a graceful degraded path: when the allocator rejects a request, return HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` windows using tokenized backoff keys (per-tenant) not global. That way clients can back off without thundering herd.

sasha: Tokenized backoff sounds good. We should use exponential backoff with jitter but bounded min/max. Suggest config: ```backoff:{ \"base_seconds\":1, \"max_seconds\":30, \"jitter\":0.25 }``` and server returns `X-Backoff-Key: tenant-<id>-v2` so retries are aligned per-tenant.

maya: Metrics to add before rollout: `peering_backoff_count{tenant,tier}`, `peering_eviction_count{tenant,tier}`, `ephemeral_lease_ms{tenant,tier}`. We can alert on >5% eviction rate for enterprise in a 5m window.

alex: Ops note: making allocator stateful increases DB calls. We can cache score in-memory and only persist on pin/unpin events to avoid thundering on every allocation. Cache TTL 30s should be fine.

liam: Security check: header-based priorities could be spoofed. Ensure we validate priority on control-plane authn or derive tier from customer metadata service — header can be advisory only.

sasha: Good catch. We'll canonicalize priority on the control-plane side using the tenant token. Connectors should send `X-Tenant-ID` and a signed `X-Tenant-Signature` header we verify. Only then we accept pinned=true.

maya: Rollout plan: 1) add metrics and tokens + 429 backoff in staging; 2) implement scoring + pinned support behind feature flag; 3) canary allocator in staging; 4) enable for 10% customers in prod with enterprise-only pins; 5) monitor eviction and latency, then broaden.

alex: Ops checklist: DB migration to add `pinned_sessions` table (tenant_id, expires_at, lease_id), allocator config knobs, and a read-through cache. Also migration for operator to set pinned flag during Dedicated onboarding.

liam: Edge-case: cross-region affinity — enterprise might have pinned sessions in us-east but requests land in us-west. We should make score calculation support regional affinity preference and fallback to cross-region peer only if score delta < threshold.

sasha: That helps reduce latency surprises. Add `region_penalty` in score: subtract 0.2 if peer region != request region.

maya: Any objections to the plan? If not I can draft an RFC follow-up with config snippets and the canary cut plan.

alex: No objections. One more: add e2e test that simulates pool drain and asserts enterprise handshakes succeed while lower-tier fall back.

liam: I'll handle the test harness and metrics dashboard queries.

sasha: I'll own the allocator changes + signature verification glue.

maya: Great — will write the RFC and drop links here. Thanks. :thumbsup:
